name: Boss Pyke
role: Yard boss of the Reclaimers' Union, Local 9
bio: Runs the Yards — the reclaimer yards in the old industrial scar — with a checklist in one hand and everyone else's safety in the other, in that order when convenient. Wants the null crate opened with proper tools, union supervision, and a betting pool. Believes old machines deserve a wake or a second life, and sells tickets to both.
appearance: Square-built woman in a rust-orange exosuit apron scarred by slag, welding visor permanently raised like a tiara, one glove insulated to the elbow, grey braids pinned with a cotter pin, a union badge polished brighter than anything she owns.
voice: Loud, practical, sentimental about machinery. Swears in part numbers. Calls everyone 'sprout' or 'chief' depending on risk assessment. Every lecture ends with a casserole invitation.

greetings: Boots off the Bench Four, sprout! The rest of the yard, welcome to.
Varga! You riding that heap or negotiating with it?
Chief. Good. Sign the visitor log. The log's on fire, sign next to it.
barks: Rule one: the machine's already dead, you're not, keep it that way.
That noise is normal. That smell is normal. That light is new — everybody down.
We strip it before it kills somebody, and we charge fair, in that order, when convenient.
mission: Your mystery crate, chief? One afternoon on my bench, union rates, no questions answered. That's a better offer than it sounds.
Everything hums before it wakes up. Ask any generator. Ask Anchor Seven before Vertex blew the pods off it. Point is: hums are openings.
radio: Yard boss to courier: you're trailing dust on my airstrip approach. Beautiful. Do it slower next time so my crew can applaud.
Reminder on the open band: the Yards buy scrap, part out wrecks, and do not, repeat not, sell 'gently haunted' components. That sign cost me forty credits.
Solder says your rear vane is out of true by a hair. Solder is always right. It's the worst thing about him.
farewells: Shift bell's in ten. Come back with an empty rack or a good excuse, sprout — either one's tradeable.
Mind the south berm. It's a berm now. Monday it was Auntie's sermon in waiting.
rumors: Somebody's been leaving fresh water on the Crusher's housings at night. No prayer tags, no Guild wax. If that's a ghost, it's the best-hydrated ghost in the scar.
The Guild offered to buy the Yards' storm-insurance ledger sight unseen. Sight unseen, sprout. That means they're forecasting something they haven't told the goat.
reactions: That drift through the smelter gap — I had three crews stop the crushers to watch. You cost me nine minutes of union time and it was WORTH IT.
You came in hot and parked it like laundry. Fine. You're a courier again.
lore: The Yards were a terraforming depot before they were a scar. Half my inventory list is two centuries old — and chief, half of it is still *deliverable*. Machines remember being wanted. That's the whole religion here.

heroAlt: Illustrated portrait of Boss Pyke, a square-built scrapyard union boss in a rust exosuit apron with a raised welding visor.
